newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Skiers recall horror of Swiss cable car crash.
newsitem.headline: Skiers recall horror of Swiss cable car crash.

text.p: Skiers screamed and feared for their lives when a malfunction sent their cable cars crashing onto a Swiss mountainside at the weekend, crushing a local guide.

Authorities blamed a broken axle on a giant winch for suddenly releasing tension on the cable, sending three gondolas plummeting to the ground on Saturday at Riederalp in the southwestern canton of Valais.
Eighteen people were injured, two of them seriously.
"It was terrible," Fritz Mueller, 61, told the SonntagsBlick newspaper. "We plunged without any warning. Everyone was screaming. We hit the ground several times and then were catapulted back up."
His daughter Silvia added: "I screamed the whole time. And I thought: This is the end. I am going to die."
Former Swiss ski acrobat Art Furrer, who owns a hotel in the resort, skied down the mountain after the accident to comfort the injured Swiss and German skiers.
"Most of the people in the gondolas were covered with blood," he told the newspaper.
At one point he found a pair of ski boots under one car. They belonged to his friend Franz-Xaver Leiggener, 36, a local ski instructor and mountain guide who was crushed to death.

"Six passengers were thrown from one gondola when it hit the ground the first time. When it hit the second time, one of these people, the mountain guide, was crushed," he added in an interview with the SonntagsZeitung weekly.
Technical experts were puzzled by the accident. The cable system had been in operation only one year and used the most modern technology.
"Until yesterday i thought such an accident was impossible," said Ulrich Boesiger, president of the Swiss Cable Car Association's technical committee.

"Weight-bearing parts like the broken axle are subject to strict controls. There are cable cars where these parts have worked perfectly for 35 years and still have not had to be replaced," he told SonntagsBlick..
Victims were flown by helicopter to hospitals in the area after the accident around 0900 GMT.
